name: What soft costs are usually missed in a home build estimate?

mainEntity.name: Which soft costs do homeowners commonly forget when planning a new build or major remodel?
mainEntity.text: Which soft costs do homeowners commonly forget when planning a new build or major remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Soft costs are one of the biggest reasons budgets run short. Homeowners often focus on the construction number and forget the expenses needed to get the project ready to build. In Los Angeles-area projects, that can include architect fees, structural and civil engineering, survey work, soils and geotechnical reports, permit and plan check fees, energy compliance, appraisal costs, financing charges, utility upgrades, temporary services, and sometimes owner’s contingency. Soft costs are especially important for custom homes and additions because they can add a large amount before construction starts. A proper estimate should show soft costs separately from hard construction costs so the owner can see the full project budget. If those items are missing, the estimate is incomplete and the total project cost will be understated.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commonly missed soft costs include design fees, engineering, surveys, soils reports, permit fees, plan check charges, energy compliance, insurance, financing costs, and utility connection fees. These can add a meaningful amount before construction even starts.
